claims.text: SQUID magnetometry with magnetic susceptibility measurements can detect the presence of ferromagnetic ground states.
The material is ferromagnetic at low temperature.
Magnetic susceptibility should be measured using SQUID magnetometry.
The measurement is conducted at low temperature and magnetic fields up to 1 T.
Magnetic-moment alignment is the structural mediator associated with the ferromagnetic state.
Magnetic-moment alignment can be detected through changes in magnetic susceptibility.
A ferromagnetic ground state will produce a 20% increase in magnetic susceptibility relative to the stated baseline.
The relevant experimental domain is 0–10 K and 0–1 T.
Other magnetic interactions may interfere with the susceptibility signature.
Failure to observe at least a 15% susceptibility increase relative to the baseline at 0 K falsifies the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The initial state presupposes a ferromagnetic material, while the baseline describes the material without ferromagnetic ground states; no distinct control material, phase, or perturbation that realizes this baseline is specified.
